h.select_rule: Choose 10 that together cover the most distinct mechanisms, edit fields and condition fields; prefer clear, falsifiable claims that go beyond well-known findings yet have a concrete mechanistic rationale; include both directions; drop near-duplicates and claims merely restating main effects.
h.strategy: Use the retrieved literature to identify what is already well established about main effects, then deliberately go one step further: propose conditional effects the literature implies but does not directly test, or where findings conflict. Draw on general mechanisms such as redundancy, bottlenecks, saturation, interference between components and compensation. Span many different edit and condition fields, propose some LOWER-direction hypotheses where a common edit is predicted to help less, and make each 'why' specific enough that a single comparison could refute it.

hyps.why: Edge 2 is dead when edge 0 is none (node 1 has no input), so the edit's effect is near zero and lower than when edge 0 is active.
Edge 4 carries nothing when node 1 is disconnected, so a conv3x3 there has no effect, lower than when edge 0 is active.
With edge 0 removed, edge 1 is the only input to node 2, so a conv3x3 there is the cell's only learned feature extractor.
With edge 1 removed, edge 5's only source is the 0->1->2 chain, so a conv3x3 there is the main learned transformation of that route.
A conv3x3 on edge 1 already gives a strong learned path to node 2, so adding conv3x3 on edge 0 gains less (saturation).
With a skip on edge 3 providing the identity path, a conv3x3 on edge 4 adds less.
A skip on edge 3 compensates for a deep conv chain by adding an identity path, helping more when edge 5 is a conv3x3.
With no direct edge 3, learned capacity must come through intermediate nodes, so conv3x3 on edge 0 matters more.
Removing edge 0 hurts far more when edge 3 is also none, because only the 0->2->3 route to the output then remains.
Replacing the identity skip with a pool blurs features and removes the clean gradient path, hurting accuracy.
